scenes.headline: How two LoRAs teach a 3D generator about soles
scenes.sub: Hugging Face's fine-tuning guide for TRELLIS.2
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Insole! Hugging Face published a guide to fine-tuning a 3D generator. It is about one model and one kind of object, and that is what makes it useful.

steps.say: TRELLIS.2 turns a photo into a mesh in three stages, each a flow transformer reading the same image tokens.

steps.term: Sparse structure: which voxels are object
steps.say: Stage one decides which voxels are part of the object at all. Its coarse shape.
Stage two makes the surface geometry for every occupied cell. The sole lives here.
Stage three paints the materials. The guide leaves it frozen.

scenes.title: Why the texture stage stays frozen

left.title: What the scans have
items: Diffuse colour with lighting baked in
No separate roughness or metallic maps
left.say: The scans only have colour with the lighting baked in.

right.title: What the error is
items: The soles are wrong, not the colours
So adapt the two geometry stages
right.say: And the error is in the soles, not the colours. So only the geometry stages get adapters.

scenes.title: What one adapter adds to a layer

parts.note: two thin matrices of rank r
parts.say: The adapter learns two thin matrices whose product is the update.

parts.note: B starts at zero, so training starts from the base
parts.say: B starts at zero, so training begins exactly at the base model.

scenes.say: LoRA adds a low rank update to each targeted layer.

scenes.label: parameters in each released adapter, read from its safetensors header
scenes.note: the guide says 9.3 million for both
scenes.say: I read the two released adapters' headers. Each holds nine point three million parameters. The guide says that number covers both. It covers one.

steps.say: The data is a hundred and eighty-eight scanned shoes from Google Scanned Objects.
TRELLIS.2's own frozen encoders turn each mesh into latents once, so every run reuses them.
Blender renders sixteen views of each shoe, and training picks one at random as the input photo.
Nine shoes are held out, with their other colourways kept out of training too.
Then one run per adapter on an A100. The guide's runs took seven point two and three point six hours.
Now the scores. The evaluation centres and scales each mesh, but never rotates it. A shoe lying on its side scores badly even if its shape is right.
Turn the base output upright, and on five held-out shoes its F-score climbs to nearly half. That part was pose.

steps.term: F-score: surface within two percent, both ways
steps.say: The LoRA reaches about nought point eight five on the same five. That gap is the sole.
The guide's own figure shows both: the base as generated, then at its best rotation.
And with the adapters, next to the scan.

items.say: The headline says F-score went from about a quarter to about four fifths.
Part of that is the adapters learning to stand shoes the way the scans stand.

items.text: Part of it is the sole
items.say: The rest is better soles, which is the part the guide was after.

scenes.text: Pick the stage your error lives in, freeze the rest, and align before you score.
scenes.say: Pick the stage your error lives in, freeze the rest, and align your meshes before you score them.

recap: Adapters on the two geometry flows
Texture frozen: the scans bake in light
scenes.say: Two geometry adapters, a frozen texture stage, and pose and shape scored apart.
